skill.name: snowtower-admin
skill.description: Manage SnowTower Snowflake infrastructure with guidance for SnowDDL deployments, user provisioning, role grants, CI/CD releases, troubleshooting, and security operations.
skill.summary: SnowTower administration guide for SnowDDL deployments, Snowflake users, roles, CI/CD, troubleshooting, and security operations.
skill.author: Database-Tycoon

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and code fences. Confirmed risks remain around sensitive Snowflake key handling, .env guidance, ACCOUNTADMIN usage, and an emergency account without network policy.

remediation.issue: Sensitive Snowflake private key handling is described without strict agent consent boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Add instructions that agents must never read private keys, .env files, or GitHub secrets unless the user explicitly approves that exact action.

remediation.issue: Emergency access guidance documents a named account without network policy.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the named account with a placeholder and require break-glass controls, MFA, logging, expiration, and post-use review.

remediation.issue: ACCOUNTADMIN is recommended for multiple routine troubleshooting and environment workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Document least-privilege role alternatives and reserve ACCOUNTADMIN for narrow, approved operations only.

remediation.issue: Emergency commands can suspend warehouses, roll back deployments, rotate keys, and update secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Require environment confirmation, plan review, change ticket reference, and human approval before high-impact commands run.

semantic_findings.title: Emergency Account Without Network Policy
semantic_findings.description: The guide states that STEPHEN_RECOVERY is configured without a network policy and uses password authentication. This creates a standing emergency access bypass that could be targeted or misused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly names an emergency account, says it has no network policy, and says it uses password authentication.

semantic_findings.description: The guide recommends ACCOUNTADMIN for troubleshooting and sets SNOWFLAKE_ROLE to ACCOUNTADMIN in required environment settings. Routine use of the top account role increases blast radius for mistakes.

content.value_statement: Snowflake administration requires careful control of users, roles, deployments, and security settings. This skill gives structured SnowTower guidance for SnowDDL operations.
actual_capabilities: Guides SnowDDL planning and deploy-safe workflows for infrastructure changes.
Explains Snowflake user creation with encrypted passwords and RSA key setup.
Describes business roles, technical roles, schema roles, and grant structure.
Outlines database, schema, warehouse, and network policy configuration patterns.
Supports CI/CD release workflows, troubleshooting, MFA checks, and cost operations.
limitations: It is a Markdown guide and does not include executable helper scripts.
It assumes an existing SnowTower repository with SnowDDL commands installed.
It cannot verify account-specific permissions without access to the target environment.
Some procedures involve secrets or production changes and require human approval.

use_cases.title: Plan Infrastructure Changes
use_cases.description: Preview SnowDDL changes, review grants, and prepare a safe deployment path before applying updates.

use_cases.title: Provision Snowflake Users
use_cases.description: Create user entries, choose authentication patterns, assign business roles, and prepare encrypted credential fields.

use_cases.title: Resolve Production Issues
use_cases.description: Investigate grant drift, authentication failures, locked users, warehouse status, and MFA compliance checks.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare a SnowDDL plan review for a small user or role change. List the checks I should perform before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a User Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through adding a Snowflake user in SnowTower. Include role selection, authentication choice, and review steps before applying changes.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Grant Drift
prompt_templates.prompt: A SnowDDL plan shows many unexpected revokes. Help me diagnose schema grant drift and choose a safe remediation path.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Emergency Runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a controlled SnowTower emergency runbook for rollback or service account reset. Include approval gates, logging, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Plan the onboarding of a new analyst user.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering user details, business role selection, authentication method, encrypted password handling, plan review, and deployment approval.

output_examples.input: Investigate unexpected revoke statements in a deployment plan.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting path that checks schema grant drift, validates expected ownership, and recommends using the safer deployment wrapper.

output_examples.input: Prepare a controlled service account reset.
output_examples.output: A staged procedure with approval, key regeneration, Snowflake update, secret rotation, validation, and post-incident documentation.

best_practices: Run a plan review before every SnowDDL deployment and inspect drops, revokes, and admin role changes.
Use least-privilege roles for routine work and reserve ACCOUNTADMIN for approved exceptions.
Treat .env files, private keys, Fernet keys, and GitHub secrets as sensitive material.
anti_patterns: Do not apply SnowDDL changes without reviewing the generated plan first.
Do not let an agent read private keys, .env files, or secrets without explicit approval.
Do not use emergency accounts or production reset commands as routine administration tools.

faq.question: What is SnowTower Admin for?
faq.answer: It helps administrators manage Snowflake infrastructure through SnowTower and SnowDDL workflows.

faq.question: Does it run commands by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command examples that users must review before execution.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create Snowflake users?
faq.answer: It explains user provisioning patterns, role assignment, encrypted passwords, and RSA key setup.

faq.question: What should I review before deployment?
faq.answer: Review planned creates, alters, drops, grants, revokes, admin role changes, and schema grant drift.

faq.question: What security precautions are required?
faq.answer: Use least privilege, protect secrets, confirm environments, and require human approval for high-impact actions.
